rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to capture all 6 compounds without truncation and map the overall elution window. This run should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, held late, or distributed across the gradient so later injections can trim the window and adjust slope.

All pairs are vastly over-resolved, so the score is now limited by analysis time; the first run suggests the elution window is roughly phi_e 0.18 to 0.68. Narrowing the gradient to that window, shortening tG, and raising T should pull the last peak toward 10 min while still leaving ample resolution margin.

We already have full resolution, so push harder on speed to bring the last peak under 10 min. A slightly higher phi1 and temperature with a shorter gradient should accelerate the late peak substantially, while the current worst pair still has enough margin to likely remain resolved.

CRF is already maximal, so this is a boundary probe to see whether the method can be made even faster while keeping all pairs at or above 1.5. Shortening tG and raising T should stress the current weakest early pair (1,2) and reveal how much speed margin remains.

The fast method failed only on the earliest pair, so lower phi0 while keeping the same steep late end to selectively give compounds 1 and 2 more retention and spacing without sacrificing much total time. This directly tests whether the weak pair is controlled more by the low-organic start than by overall gradient length.

Lowering phi0 improved the critical early pair, so the next efficient lever is a slightly shallower gradient at the same high temperature. Extending tG from 6 to 8 min should push pair (1,2) above 1.5 while likely keeping t_last under 10 min, which would recover a CRF of 1.0 with a faster method than injection 3.

The shift from 55 to 60 C changed which pair is limiting, showing temperature strongly affects selectivity; backing off temperature one step from the proven 1.0 method should test whether a cooler run keeps all pairs resolved while preserving t_last under 10 min. If so, this could define a wider robust optimum around the current best settings.

Interpolation between the successful 8 min/55 C run and the overcompressed 6 min/60 C run should show whether 6 min is salvageable at a slightly lower temperature. This directly targets a potentially faster 1.0-CRF method while keeping the gradient window already shown to work.

Now that 6 min at 55 C still gives full credit with some margin, the next logical boundary test is 4 min at the same window and temperature. This will show whether the method can be shortened further before the early critical pair drops below R = 1.5.

The 4 min run lost score only on the earliest pair, and lowering phi0 previously improved that pair, so keep the ultrafast format but start at lower organic. This should selectively restore early spacing while preserving the strong late elution and very short total run.

A narrower gradient window should reduce steepness and can recover the critical early resolution while likely keeping all peaks well within 10 minutes, since the last peak already elutes by 6.7 minutes at phi1 0.70. This tests whether phi1 0.65 preserves full resolution in the faster 6-minute format and could give a more efficient robust optimum.

Since narrowing the window to phi1 0.65 improved the 6-minute method while keeping full resolution, the next step is to test whether that gentler 4-minute gradient can still hold the critical early pair above 1.5. This probes for an even shorter maximum-CRF method using the most promising window found so far.

At the promising 0.15–0.65, 6 min window, raising temperature one step tests whether the method can be made even faster without losing the full-resolution threshold. The previous 6 min/0.15–0.70 run at 60 C only failed on the early pair, so the narrower window may offset that compression enough to retain CRF 1.0.

The limiting pair remains the very first one, and raising phi0 should delay the earliest compounds into a less compressed part of the gradient while simultaneously narrowing the window and keeping the run short. This tests whether a slightly stronger starting solvent positioning can outperform the current 6-minute 1.0 methods on robustness without sacrificing full credit.

Reducing phi1 from 0.65 to 0.60 further narrows the gradient window and should make the 6-minute slope shallower, which may boost the limiting early-pair resolution while still likely eluting the last peak well before 10 minutes. This is a targeted optimization around the successful 0.15–0.65, 6 min, 55 C method.

The 0.15–0.60 window improved the limiting early pair at 6 minutes, so it is the best candidate to rescue a 4-minute method. This run tests whether the shallower 4-minute gradient in the tighter window can keep all pairs at or above 1.5 while cutting total analysis time further.

The 4-minute 0.15–0.60 method is extremely close to full credit, missing only slightly on pair (1,2), and lowering temperature has consistently improved that pair. Dropping from 55 to 50 C should add just enough selectivity/retention to push R above 1.5 while still keeping the last peak well under 10 minutes.

Now that a 4-minute method reaches CRF 1.0, the remaining optimization is to trim the gradient window further without letting the last peak exceed 10 minutes or the early pair fall below 1.5. Lowering phi1 one step should make the slope shallower and may preserve or improve the critical resolution while still likely eluting the last compound in time.

The 0.15–0.55, 4 min, 50 C method still gives full credit with margin and the last peak remains below 10 min, so one more reduction in phi1 probes the lowest usable upper bound. This will test whether the tighter window can still keep all six compounds fully resolved while staying inside the 10-minute t_last target.

The drop from phi1 0.55 to 0.50 showed the late compound is highly sensitive to the upper bound, so phi1 0.55 is near the practical minimum. Raising temperature one step at that successful window should pull the last peak back toward a shorter run while the ample current resolution margin suggests all pairs should remain above 1.5.

The current 0.15–0.55, 4-minute method still has resolution margin and an 8.4-minute last peak, so one final temperature increase cleanly probes the speed limit at this optimized window. This should determine whether the method can be made still faster while retaining full resolution, or whether 55 C is the true boundary.

At 0.15–0.55, 4 min, 55 C the only risky pair is still the first one, and lowering phi0 has previously improved that pair without hurting late elution much. This tests whether the same ultrafast window can gain extra early-pair margin and define a more robust maximum-CRF method.

Lowering phi0 at 55 C gave a robust 4-minute maximum-CRF method, and dropping temperature one step should further increase the margin on the critical first pair while still keeping t_last comfortably below 10 minutes. This is a final robustness check near the best ultrafast operating point.

With only two injections left, test an unexplored corner that could combine the strong early-pair benefit of low phi0 with the faster late elution of a slightly higher phi1 at high temperature. This checks whether 4 minutes at 60 C can still reach full resolution when the window is widened just enough to help the last peak.

The 0.10–0.60, 4 min method was just below full credit at 55 C and failed badly at 60 C only because the first pair compressed, so lowering temperature one step below 50 C is the best remaining chance to find a still faster robust 1.0 method in this high-phi1 window. If successful, it would match the 4-minute format with stronger late elution than the 0.55 upper bound.
